mappings.note: The iris or pupil controlling light entering the eye is eye structure and function; not LO-170, no optical phenomenon outside the eye.
Correcting myopia with a concave lens is science applied to a real need; not LO-169, a correction rather than the cause of the defect.
Light entering through the cornea or pupil is eye structure; grouped with the eye-anatomy items.
Finding the angle of reflection for a 30 degree incidence is the angle outcome named verbatim in LO-172; not LO-170, an angle rather than an image.
Left and right swapping in a mirror is lateral inversion, part of explaining image formation; not LO-166, no mirror types contrasted.
White light splitting in a prism explains dispersion; not LO-167, nothing classified.
A rainbow showing dispersion explains a natural phenomenon; grouped with the prism item.
The blind spot as the region with no sensory cells is eye structure; grouped with the eye-anatomy items.
The angle of reflection for perpendicular incidence is the angle outcome verbatim; grouped with the other angle items.
Excluding the non-luminous object sorts objects into luminous and non-luminous; not LO-170, no phenomenon explained.
What is needed to build a kaleidoscope is constructing a model from materials at hand, which LO-175 covers; not LO-170, which is used where the multiple-image principle itself is asked.
Cones as the colour-sensing cells is eye structure and function; not LO-166, no contrast with rods being drawn.
An owl seeing at night because of many rods and few cones relates an ability to its cause; not LO-174, an explanation rather than plain anatomy.
Seeing an object because light reaches the eye explains vision; not LO-174, the light rather than the eye's parts being the point.
Light bouncing back into the same medium being reflection explains the phenomenon; not LO-172, no angle involved.
A mirror having a smooth or polished surface belongs to the explanation of reflection; not LO-166, no mirror types contrasted.
Which surface reflects most light belongs to the explanation of reflection; not LO-166, surfaces rather than image types being compared within one phenomenon.
The silvered backing of a plane mirror belongs to how a mirror reflects; grouped with the reflection items.
The perpendicular to the reflecting surface being the normal is the reference line for the angles LO-172 names; not LO-170, the geometry rather than the image.
How many laws of reflection there are concerns the angle rules; grouped with the other angle items.
The angle of incidence always being equal to the angle of reflection is LO-172 verbatim; grouped with the other angle items.
The angle between reflected ray and normal being the angle of reflection is LO-172's own subject; grouped with the angle items.
Reflection from a smooth surface being regular reflection explains the phenomenon; not LO-172, no angle measured.
What produces diffused reflection explains the phenomenon; grouped with the regular-reflection item.
The nature of a plane-mirror image explains image formation; not LO-166, no mirror types contrasted.
The pen changing hands in the mirror image is lateral inversion; duplicate in substance of the dressing-table item.
The number of images between mirrors inclined at 40 degrees is the formation of multiple images, named verbatim in LO-170; not LO-172, because the count rather than an angle of reflection is asked.
Which mirror is used as a side-view mirror is choosing a device for everyday use; not LO-166, a use rather than a bare comparison.
The cornea as the bulging front of the eyeball is eye structure; duplicate in substance of the earlier cornea item.
Tracing a ray between two mirrors at right angles to find the final angle of reflection is measurement of those angles, LO-172 verbatim; not LO-170, angles rather than images being tracked.
The image of a toy lying as far behind a plane mirror as the object is in front explains image formation; not LO-172, a distance rather than an angle.
The image of a candle being the same height as the object explains image formation; grouped with the image-distance item.
Which device works by multiple reflections is the formation of multiple images verbatim; not LO-175, no model being constructed.
Braille letting visually challenged people read and write is science applied in daily life; not LO-174, an aid rather than anatomy.
How far a normal eye sees clearly is a fact about normal vision; not LO-169, no defect being traced.
The nearest distance a normal eye sees clearly is a fact about normal vision; grouped with the far-point item.
The angle between incident ray and normal being the angle of incidence is LO-172's own subject; duplicate in substance of the earlier item.
The iris contracting and dilating to control light is eye structure and function; duplicate in substance of the earlier iris item.
Dispersion as the breaking up of white light explains a phenomenon; duplicate in substance of the earlier dispersion items.
Seeing ourselves in a mirror but not on a wall turns on regular versus diffused reflection; grouped with the reflection items rather than the mirror-choice items.
